subject: Sizing follow-up: deployment mode choices & GPU / TPS tradeoffs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@blueoakhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's sizing discussion

Alex — thanks again for taking the call today. I wanted to capture the items we discussed and ask a few quick clarifying questions so we can put together a concrete Dedicated capacity plan (and quote) that compares Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC for your team. High-level recap: you need low-latency inference for clinical triage, PHI-sensitive data (so VPC/on-prem is on the table), and predictable costs for an initial rollout + burst capacity for peaks.

To size capacity precisely, could you confirm the following points? If easier, fill the attached capacity_estimate_template.xlsx and send back.

- Target peak TPS (requests/sec) and expected average TPS over a 24h window
- Typical token mix: average prompt tokens, average generated tokens, and percent of requests that are short (<=128 tokens) vs long (>=1024 tokens)
- Expected concurrency (simultaneous active sessions/streams) and any per-user QPS limits
- Preferred GPU family (H100, A100, L4) or openness to recommendations based on cost/latency tradeoffs
- Requirement for VPC/on-prem (PHI) vs Hosted API acceptable for non-PHI flows
- Any SLA/uptime targets or max request latency SLOs (p50/p95) we should budget for

I can produce three scenarios: (A) Hosted API with autoscale, (B) Dedicated reserved pool with suggested GPU mix, and (C) Private VPC + SOW for initial on-prem pilot. We'll include estimated monthly spend, warm cache recommendations, and quantization options.

Next steps: if you can reply with the numbers above or the completed spreadsheet by EOD Friday (5/29), I'll have an initial capacity worksheet and a draft SOW for review by early next week. If you'd prefer a 20-minute follow-up, I'm happy to schedule one.

Attachments: capacity_estimate_template.xlsx

Thanks —
Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

--
Redwood Inference — production-ready LLM inference for engineering teams
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@blueoakhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T18:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's sizing discussion

Soojin — thanks for the recap and the template. Answers below (happy to expand if helpful):

- Peak TPS: ~1,200 requests/sec during morning surge (08:00–10:00 PT)
- Average TPS: ~140 requests/sec across the day
- Token mix: average prompt ~230 tokens, average response ~480 tokens. Estimated distribution: 55% short (<=128 tokens), 30% medium (129–1024), 15% long (>=1024).
- Concurrency: we expect ~320 concurrent sessions during peak, with most sessions issuing 1–3 requests/sec. Global concurrent clients (simultaneous users) could reach ~1,100, but active inference concurrency is closer to 320 due to backoff/idle behavior.
- GPU preference: we'd prefer H100-class if latency-critical, but we're cost-conscious — please show H100 vs A100 comparisons. We're curious about smaller inference-optimized L4-style instances for lower-cost non-critical traffic.
- PHI/data residency: we must keep PHI in a customer-controlled VPC for production. Non-PHI experimentation can use Hosted.
- Latency SLOs: target p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms for the typical prompt sizes above.

I've attached our completed security questionnaire and a short note from infra on expected QPS per client. Happy to hop on a short follow-up if you need to walk through anything.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering | BlueOak Health
alex.mercer@blueoakhealth.com
Attachments: security_questionnaire_blueoak.pdf
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@blueoakhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-23T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's sizing discussion

Alex — this is perfect, thank you. We'll produce: 1) a three-scenario capacity worksheet (Hosted / Dedicated reserved / Private VPC) with recommended GPU mix and costs, 2) a comparison matrix showing expected p50/p95 under each GPU choice (H100/A100/L4 quantized), and 3) a draft SOW for a Private pilot that includes data residency and SOC2 controls.

Immediate asks for you: if you have a few example requests (anonymized) with token counts and the time-of-day distribution, that will let us simulate real token throughput and KV cache hit improvements.

Plan and timeline: we'll get the initial worksheet and SOW to you by end of day Monday (5/25). Aditya, Evelyn — looping you in to prepare the Dedicated sizing options (GPU counts, recommended instance SKUs, and an initial pricing band). I'll include a short appendix on warm cache sizing and average token throughput assumptions.

Thanks again — talk soon.

Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-23T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BlueOak answers — action items for Dedicated sizing

Aditya / Evelyn — forwarding Alex's answers. Key asks:
- Produce a Dedicated reserved pool option sized for peak ~1,200 TPS with an expected active concurrency of ~320 (include options for H100 vs A100 and quantized L4 alternatives).
- Provide per-GPU instance counts and a suggested warm KV cache configuration; estimate cold vs warm startup impact on p95.
- Prepare a 3-tier pricing band (Conservative, Expected, Aggressive) and note any assumptions about burst capacity and autoscale windows.
- Confirm whether we can meet p50 < 120ms / p95 < 400ms on H100 for the token profiles Alex gave; if not, list tradeoffs.

Attachments to include in the customer packet: capacity_estimate_template.xlsx, SOW-draft-blueoak-v1.pdf. I also attached their security questionnaire.

Can you aim to have a first pass slide + worksheet by EOD Monday so we can send to BlueOak on Tuesday?

Thanks —
Soojin
